Subject: Sudden throughput collapse / 5xx spike on our private cluster (please escalate)

Kimberly —

We're seeing a major degradation on our on-prem Redwood deployment in our primary US region starting ~08:40 PT this morning. Symptoms:
- Throughput down ~60% vs baseline for user inference QPS.
- 5xx rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% (majority 502/504).
- P95 token latency increased from ~180ms to >2.5s.

This started shortly after we applied the runtime package 1.12.3-rc and a batching policy tweak (max_batch_bytes lowered to 1.2MB). We rolled both into our canary and then to all nodes at ~07:30.

I've attached a short snapshot of pod logs and the perf graphs. Ops is seeing KV cache miss rates spike and queue lengths grow. The degradation is customer-facing — several clinics have reported timeouts.

We need Redwood to urgently:
1) Confirm whether 1.12.3-rc contains any changes to KV cache eviction or kernel-level I/O that could explain the burst.
2) Recommend an immediate mitigation (rollback vs config tweak) we can apply with minimal customer disruption.
3) Senior engineering/ops presence — our CTO is asking for an executive summary and next steps.

Please escalate to SRE/Platform. If someone can join a call now that would be great — tagging Kimberly as our Redwood contact.

Sara

Joining — quick triage notes after an initial look at the snapshots Sara sent:
- Pod-level: several worker pods show repeated decoder OOM and restarts clustered around 08:42. k8s pod snapshot attached (k8s-pods-snapshot-09014.txt).
- Runtime config: our diff tool shows two changes between 1.12.2 -> 1.12.3-rc that look potentially relevant:
  * kv_cache.max_entries default decreased by 30%
  * internal batching algorithm now prefers smaller batch thresholds under memory pressure (this can increase request fanout)
- Observed behavior: high cache miss rate + increased inter-node traffic — suggests KV eviction leading to more remote cache fetches and higher latency.

Immediate recommended steps:
1) Rollback runtime on 20% of nodes (canary) to 1.12.2 and watch 5xx and p95 for 10 minutes.
2) If rollback helps, expand to global rollback during your maintenance window.
3) If rollback is not possible or slow, restore kv_cache.max_entries to previous value via config (hot reload supported) and revert max_batch_bytes change.

I've attached runtime-config-diff-20280914.json with the exact flags. Jonas — any additional low-level checks we should run now?

Thanks — dug into the logs and kernel metrics from the snapshots. My read:
- The runtime-level change to kv_cache sizing reduced on-heap entries, which increased lookups to remote peers. That caused more synchronous I/O and higher lock contention in the memcpy path.
- We also see an uptick in context-switches and syscall latency starting immediately after the runtime upgrade. I suspect a subtle interaction between our memory allocator tune and the newer kernel I/O path (RCU/async writes).

Hotfix options (ranked):
A) Hot reload config: restore kv_cache.max_entries to prior value (this is fast and should immediately reduce remote fetches).
B) Canary rollback of runtime (1.12.2) on a subset of nodes to validate root cause; rollback is straightforward but will take ~25–35 minutes to complete cluster-wide.
C) Kernel tunables: temporarily increase vm.swappiness and bump net.core.somaxconn to reduce accept queue saturation — lower confidence and requires infra coordination.

Command (safe) to run for quick check:
- curl -sS http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep kv_cache_miss_rate
Expected improvement if fix works: kv_cache_miss_rate down to <= 1.0 per second per node, p95 back < 300ms.

I'll prepare an exact rollback runbook and a minimal patch to restore kv_cache config. Putting the runbook in the Drive link and creating JIRA OPS-11234 for tracking.

—Jonas

- We applied Marissa's hot reload to restore kv_cache.max_entries on a small shard at 10:14 PT; that shard's p95 dropped from 2.6s -> 210ms and 5xx fell to 0.3% within 7 minutes.
- Based on that, we approved an incremental cluster-wide config restore at 14:00 PT which stabilized the fleet.

1) Formal RCA and executive note for our CTO (we will need a short timeline and root cause that we can share with internal stakeholders).
2) Proposal for an SLA credit or goodwill consideration for the downtime window (we had two clinics escalated).

Appreciate the quick support. Evelyn/Kimberly — please send the exec summary and any comms templates. Jonas/Marissa/Marcus — can you prioritize the patch and target a candidate build next week?
